title: Expression portability of reported NR4A3-fusion targets in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma
abstract: Genes regulated by an NR4A3 fusion in an experimental model need not provide consistent RNA readouts in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) tumors. We asked how expression of three genes with published NR4A3-fusion DNA-binding evidence varied across public EMC cohorts and comparator histologies. We classified the original experimental evidence and examined expression, comparator sensitivity and discovery-data reuse. ENO3 remained elevated across the reported expression checks, including comparisons restricted by histology and reference pool. Its prior designation as a positive control means that its basic elevation is not an independent discovery. PPARG's strongest array result reused its discovery dataset. SEMA3C changed direction with the comparator histology, limiting a general claim of elevation in EMC. As a complementary analysis, the three fusion-binding genes were pooled with sixteen native-NR4A3 targets to meet the scoring method's minimum set size. This heterogeneous group did not exceed the random-set threshold on either array platform, whereas a published EMC expression signature exceeded both. Our bounded search retrieved no NR4A3-fusion DNA-binding measurements in EMC material. Surrogate occupancy comparisons concerned other proteins or tissues, and their two nominal hits did not survive multiple-testing correction. The findings distinguish consistent from comparator-dependent RNA associations among these candidates. They support ENO3's expression portability within the examined cohorts, while leaving fusion causation unresolved.
